section_summary: This section covers inquiries about shares in Japanese associations and a South African national’s sterling bonds, alongside State Department guidance on Japanese bonds held by Swiss nationals. It also records a Japan–sterling area payments amendment and a memorandum assessing British and American positions on most-favored-nation treatment for Japan.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning shares in Japanese export associations
subfiles.to: Office of Foreign Liquidation Commission, Department of State
subfiles.about: The firm asks how its client can value and liquidate shares in four Japanese associations.
subfiles.summary: Requests asset dispositions, current share values, and liquidation procedures.

subfiles.title: Request to investigate Japanese association shares
subfiles.to: Chief, United States Reparations and Restitution Delegation
subfiles.about: The Department forwards the law firm’s inquiry for investigation in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests information on association assets, share values, and liquidation.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of inquiry about Japanese association shares
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department tells the firm it has referred the inquiry to its delegation in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Promises a further reply after the delegation reports.

subfiles.title: Distribution of the occupied Japan revolving fund agreement
subfiles.about: The United States permits restricted circulation of a May 1948 revolving fund agreement to Far Eastern Commission members.
subfiles.summary: Approves restricted distribution of the agreement with American banks.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on circulating the revolving fund agreement
subfiles.about: Claxton records the consultations behind his approval of restricted distribution.
subfiles.summary: Army, State, and Export-Import Bank officials raised no objection; Claxton approved circulation as a restricted Far Eastern Commission document.

subfiles.title: Currency arrangement between Japan and the Sterling Area
subfiles.about: Sebald forwards an amendment allowing Japanese cotton textiles to be sold to sterling area buyers entirely for sterling.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the August 17 payments memorandum.

subfiles.title: Payments arrangements for trade between Japan and the Sterling Area
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Head of the United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: The memorandum amends the sterling area trade arrangement and states how acquired sterling may be used.
subfiles.summary: Provides for sterling settlement of participating trade and use or conversion of acquired sterling.

subfiles.title: Further information needed on Japanese association assets
subfiles.about: The delegation requests identifying details before investigating the law firm’s client’s shares.
subfiles.summary: Seeks association names in romaji and Japanese, purchase dates, and registered-owner names.

subfiles.title: Reply to delegation concerning association-share inquiry
subfiles.to: Chief, United States Reparations and Restitution Delegation
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges the requested details and encloses its letter to the law firm.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a letter asking the firm to send details directly to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Request for details of Japanese association securities
subfiles.from: R. Burr Smith, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department asks the firm to supply details needed for investigation in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Requests Japanese and romaji association names, acquisition dates, and any registered-owner names.

subfiles.title: Duplicate reply to delegation concerning association-share inquiry
subfiles.to: Chief, United States Reparations and Restitution Delegation
subfiles.about: A second copy acknowledges the delegation’s request and refers to the enclosed letter.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the despatch on page 713.

subfiles.title: Interests in Japanese enterprises of South African nationals: property of Mrs. Hutchinson
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The concluding page addresses Mrs. Hutchinson’s bonds and lists two supporting enclosures.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the attached bond-policy memorandum may not cover bonds held outside Japan by a United Nations national.

subfiles.title: Information and inventory report on Mrs. Hutchinson’s property
subfiles.from: Tokyo Trust & Banking Co.; K. Simura
subfiles.about: The report records a search for Mrs. Hutchinson’s sterling bonds and related custody records.
subfiles.summary: Bank and trust-company searches found no confirmed custody record for her bonds. Missing overseas branch records prevent a definitive account of their whereabouts.

subfiles.title: Japanese pre-war foreign currency bonds
subfiles.from: Patrick H. Tansey, Civil Property Custodian
subfiles.to: Head of the United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: The memorandum explains wartime conversion of foreign currency bonds and the unresolved policy for servicing them.
subfiles.summary: Bond service awaits an overall policy. The memorandum describes yen conversions, reserved interest funds, outstanding foreign currency obligations, and possible complications for bonds located abroad.

subfiles.title: File note on Swiss bondholder inquiries
subfiles.about: A State Department officer recounts a conversation with Guy de Rham about Swiss bondholder submissions.
subfiles.summary: De Rham requested a memorandum explaining the Department’s usual referral procedure.

subfiles.title: Japanese securities held by Swiss nationals
subfiles.about: The Department advises how Swiss holders of Japanese dollar bonds should present their declarations.
subfiles.summary: The Department explains that its 1946 procedure concerned equity interests rather than bonds. It describes its assistance to bondholders and recommends sending Swiss declarations to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council. It cannot yet predict peace-treaty treatment or payment arrangements.

subfiles.title: Swiss Legation acknowledgment of bond memorandum
subfiles.about: The Legation acknowledges the Department’s September 28 guidance on Japanese securities.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Swiss authorities have been informed and thanks the Department.

subfiles.title: Duplicate file note on Swiss bondholder inquiries
subfiles.about: A second copy recounts the discussion with Guy de Rham about bondholder submissions.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the note on page 723.

subfiles.title: Duplicate memorandum on Japanese securities held by Swiss nationals
subfiles.about: A second copy advises referral of Swiss holders’ Japanese dollar-bond declarations to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the memorandum on pages 724–728. It distinguishes bonds from equity interests, describes the Department’s assistance, and recommends submitting declarations to the Council.

subfiles.title: Summary of attached report on London MFN conference
subfiles.about: The memorandum compares American and British views on most-favored-nation treatment for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The United States argued that wider Japanese trade would reduce occupation costs and that MFN would aid recovery planning. British representatives cited political opposition, fear of Japanese competition, and the lack of a yen exchange rate. The writer doubts an early agreement and emphasizes that establishing an exchange rate is central to further trade discussions. The text continues beyond the supplied final page.
